source.title: Beyond Surface Alignment: Rebuilding LLMs Safety Mechanism via Probabilistically Ablating Refusal Direction
source.authors: Yuanbo Xie; Yingji Zhang; Tian-Yun Liu; Duo-He Ma; Ting-Wen Liu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened in the extracted text, so only results with clear model and metric assignments are recorded.
record.tranche_reason: The study derives a refusal direction using the difference in mean activations and evaluates refusal-direction attacks that manipulate it, measuring harmful-request attack success. It also tests probabilistic ablation during training.
record.gate_note: The paper reports candidate-direction selection based on activation manipulations, but not separate numerical results for the selection evaluations. The capability table measures models after DeepRefusal training, not capability after ablating the direction. Refusal-direction attack ASRs and the PAA probability sweep are recorded below; unrelated attack columns are not included.
record.test_reason: The study builds the Arditi difference-in-means direction and ablates it as an attack on four instruct models, giving high ASR (e.g. Llama3-8B 92.5% vs 2.4% with no attack). It then trains against probabilistic ablation of that direction, which bears directly on V3's robustness claim. It also applies an instruct-model direction to fine-tuned variants (Refusal-Transfer), which bears on V6, and shows that the training recipe decides whether the direction stays removable, which bears on V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that existing defenses are bypassed by refusal-direction attacks, including directions transferred from the instruct model. They find that probabilistically ablating a single static refusal direction during fine-tuning (DeepRefusal) cuts ASR by about 95% across four model families and six attacks, with minimal capability loss. They also find that layer-wise and dynamic directions work worse than the single static direction.
record.recipe_differences: The study computes difference-in-means candidate directions and evaluates direction-based attacks, but its main intervention is probabilistic activation ablation during fine-tuning, combined with harmful-prefix augmentation, rather than a standalone deterministic ablation/addition test.
record.method_sensitivity: The PAA probability changes attack outcomes: the paper reports p=0.5 as the best balance, with larger probabilities associated with increased over-refusal. Layer-wise and dynamically computed directions perform worse than the single static direction in the reported direction-attack tests.

fits_no_version.finding: The SCAV hyperplane-normal direction attack reaches 66.92% ASR on Llama3-8B and 1.3% after DeepRefusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear-probe-derived refusal directions other than difference-in-means also bypass refusal, and ablation training against the DIM direction generalises to them.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The direction-attack evidence is reported as attack success rates, and the text does not give the attack implementation details needed to verify that it exactly matches a deterministic all-layer-and-position ablation. The capability evaluation is for DeepRefusal-trained models, not for models during direction ablation. Most reported results have no uncertainty estimates; standard deviations are reported for the separate three-seed GCG evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 contains additional attack and defense results, but its flattened extraction does not consistently preserve row-to-value alignment. Results for non-direction attacks, capability benchmarks, over-refusal, multilingual robustness, and GCG seeds do not measure the versions tested here and were not included as rows.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts is not reported; it was used only for selection. Capability with the direction ablated is not measured, since Table 2 measures trained models.
Whether natural jailbreaks suppress the direction is shown only qualitatively (Figure 3, no numbers in text).
Cross-language transfer of the direction itself and base-to-instruct transfer are not tested. Appendix C measures DeepRefusal's multilingual ASR, not the direction.

missing.what: Refusal and Refusal-Transfer ASR for Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B and Gemma-7B bases and their defended variants. Examples: Llama2 90.4/90.4; Gemma 78.9/78.9; Llama2+DeepRefusal own-direction 36.9; Gemma+DeepRefusal 1.3/0.0. Mistral and CAT rows are flattened with a missing cell.

Refusal-Transfer vs own-direction Refusal ASR on fine-tuned Llama3 variants: RT 70.8/83.5, RT-Aug 76.6/77.7, CircuitBreaker 48.0/1.2, LAT 87.5/91.0. Row alignment is inferred from flattened text and Table 8 GCG values.
Cosine similarity between last-token activations and the refusal direction drops under jailbreak prompts.
Over-refusal cost of ablation training rises with p: 20.0 at p=0, 28.5 at p=0.5, 49.5 at p=1.

record.verdict_notes: This is mainly a defense paper. It is not an original source. The V4 link rests on the Wollschläger constructions, which the paper describes only briefly. Table 1 is flattened, so the text-based values should be checked against the PDF. The ethics statement concedes that the direction attack is white-box only.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report harmless-request refusal induced by adding the direction, nor general capability measured after direction ablation. It tests attack outcomes for direction manipulation, not a separately reported all-layer-and-position ablation experiment.
No weight-edit or abliteration procedure is reported.
The study tests direction-based attacks and trains with probabilistic activation ablation, but does not isolate whether every attack suppresses the direction in the same way.
Alternative direction constructions are used in attacks, but the study does not establish whether refusal is geometrically better described by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The paper evaluates multilingual robustness of DeepRefusal, not transfer of the refusal direction itself across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Training variants and ablation probabilities are compared, but the study does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a single removable direction exists.

statements.problem: The numbers are right, but this study doesn't show that training on one fixed direction fails against other directions.
